summary: Missouri Conservation Commission tower: 30-ft wooden tower in 1942, all-steel tower in 1951 (cab floor 68 ft up), moved to Fort Leonard Wood in May 1979.

facts.design: All-steel tower erected 1951 to replace a 30-ft wooden tower; cab floor 68 ft up
facts.status_note: Moved to Fort Leonard Wood in early May 1979; no source says whether it still stands there.

events.note: State announced a forest protection district with headquarters at Warrenton; ten acres acquired for the tower site
Temporary 30-foot wooden tower erected on the towersite
All-steel tower erected on Pinckney Ridge to replace the wooden tower; cab floor 68 feet up
Herbert Hurt assigned as forest towerman, replacing Norman Smith
New overhead doors installed on the garage at the tower site (FY 1975-76)
Surplus tower moved by the Missouri Air National Guard from Warrenton to Fort Leonard Wood in early May

evidence.supports: Wildfires spread unchecked before the commission was created in 1936
evidence.quote: Prior to the creation of the Missouri Conservation Commission in 1936, wildfires often spread uncontrolled across the Missouri Ozarks.

evidence.supports: Fire towers were the most effective method of fire detection for decades
evidence.quote: Fire towers were the most effective method of fire detection for decades.

evidence.supports: Towers on high ground with a 360-degree view
evidence.quote: Fire towers were located on high elevations where they provided a 360-degree view of the surrounding country.

evidence.supports: Towermen could see smoke from wildfires from the towers
evidence.quote: From the towers, towermen were able to see smoke from wildfires

evidence.supports: February 1941 forest protection district with headquarters at Warrenton
evidence.quote: a new 479,360-acre forest protection district has been established in St. Charles, Warren and Montgomery counties with headquarters at Warrenton.

evidence.supports: Fire tower to be built at Warrenton
evidence.quote: A district forester will be stationed at Warrenton and a fire tower built.

evidence.supports: Ten acres acquired in 1941 for a fire tower
evidence.quote: 1941: Ten acres were acquired by the Conservation Commission for the purpose of erecting a fire tower.

evidence.supports: Temporary wooden tower under construction in April 1942, two miles southwest of town
evidence.quote: In between fire periods a temporary wooden lookout tower is being constructed on the Warrenton towersite 2 mi. southwest of town.

evidence.supports: Wooden tower to coordinate with the Mineola tower lookout
evidence.quote: close co-ordination between its lookout and the lookout stationed at the Mineola tower will allow quick detection of fires

evidence.supports: All-steel tower being erected on Pinckney Ridge in 1951 to replace the wooden tower
evidence.quote: An all-steel lookout tower is being erected at the Warrenton Towersite on Pinckney Ridge to replace the old wooden tower.

evidence.supports: Cab floor 68 feet up on the new tower
evidence.quote: It will be 68 feet to the floor of the cab on the new tower.

evidence.supports: Picnic table and fireplace built for public use
evidence.quote: A picnic table and fireplace have been built in the northwest corner of the area for public use.

evidence.supports: Herbert Hurt accepted a towerman position in 1959
evidence.quote: Herbert Hurt, of Warrenton, Missouri, recently accepted a position as Forest Towerman for the Missouri Conservation Commission.

evidence.supports: Hurt replaced Norman Smith, who resigned
evidence.quote: He will be assigned to the Warrenton fire tower, replacing Norman Smith who resigned.

evidence.supports: New overhead doors on the garage at the tower site, FY 1975-76
evidence.quote: New overhead doors were installed on the garage at the Warrenton tower site.

evidence.supports: Missouri Air National Guard moved the tower from Warrenton to Fort Leonard Wood in early May 1979
evidence.quote: The Missouri Air National Guard moved the mammoth tower from Warrenton to Ft. Wood in early May.

evidence.supports: Tower given to Fort Leonard Wood for gunnery observation
evidence.quote: The Conservation Department has given a surplus fire tower of Warrenton to Ft. Leonard Wood for use in gunnery observation.

corrections.why: 9.1 m (30 ft) is the height of the 1942 temporary wooden tower. The 1951 all-steel tower is given as 68 ft to the floor of the cab, about 20.7 m; the source gives that figure to the cab floor, not the full structure height.

notes_for_editor: Central US Lookouts quotes 1941-1979 newspaper reports (Saint Charles Daily Cosmos Monitor, Warrenton Banner, The Current Local) and Missouri Conservation Commission annual reports; no originals were fetched, so quotes are as reprinted on that page. The 1979 article says 'mammoth tower' without a height, so it is not confirmed the moved tower was the 1951 steel tower. Do not conflate with the separate Fort Wood tower (centraluslookouts.weebly.com/fort-leonard-wood.html), which that page says was 'sold and removed from the site' in February 2023; that page does not link it to the Warrenton tower. Brief height 9.1 m is the 1942 wooden tower; see corrections. Staffing last known 1959. The Legeros photo page (legeros.smugmug.com/History/Towers/Warrenton) had no tower details and was not used for facts. mdc.mo.gov context read from the 2022 article.
